scalars.scalar_value: Experience with statistics and statistical software such as SPSS or R

items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Experience with statistics and statistical software such as SPSS or R
Experience working with large databases
Experience with PET or MR or other medical images
Experience with human subjects research

The Staff Research Associate 1 serves as the key staff member responsible for data management and data analysis of PET and MRI imaging data obtained as part of SCAN, a large multicenter observational study of aging and dementia. This position handles quantitative image data extraction, database management, and statistical reporting. Additionally, the Staff Research Associate 1 supports the Berkeley Aging Cohort Study by reviewing screening results, assisting with participant scheduling, and periodically assisting during neuropsychological testing and imaging sessions. Reporting to the lab Principal Investigator, this position interacts with students, postdoctoral fellows, and other lab members to analyze brain imaging data obtained using positron emission tomography (PET), Magnetic Resonance imaging (MRI), and functional MRI (fMRI) from studies including ADNI, SCAN, POINTER Imaging, and the Berkeley Aging Cohort Study (BACS). This position uses and modifies existing software and scripts to extract quantitative data, perform statistical hypothesis testing, and generate reports.
Use existing software, modify existing software and write new software to extract quantitative data from a variety of image types.
Statistical Analysis - 10%
Use standard statistical software to perform statistical hypothesis testing
Reporting and Database Management - 20%
Prepare reports in written and graphical forms. Manage databases with results; downloads and collates data from multiple databases; assembles data into datasets suitable for analysis.
Research Collaboration - 10%
Work with other researchers and principal investigators to develop analyses and explore data.
Participant Recruitment and Testing - 35%

Assist with recruiting older individuals to the Berkeley Aging Cohort Study by reviewing results of screening questionnaires and reviewing results of neuropsychological tests to determine whether the subject has undergone substantial change; periodically performs neuropsychological testing and assists during imaging studies (MRI and PET scanning).
Familiarity with python, matlab, R or other programming languages
Familiarity with multiple operating systems, especially Linus/Unix
Strong organizational skills, detail-oriented, good record-keeping
Ability to work independently and reliably
Good interpersonal skills and communication ability
